correctness.rationale: With distinct floors, a larger floor cannot be overtaken by a smaller floor under quota rounding. Within each floor block strict fractional orders force a top-residue suffix selection; outcomes thus correspond exactly to count triples 0≤tb≤mb, sum=k. The 0–1 marginal matrix M has one normalization row plus party-specific suffix indicators. Up to permutations, all positive three-part size triples with total n≤5 are (1,1,1),(2,1,1),(2,2,1),(3,1,1), and 13 displayed ±1 minors certify full column rank for all nontrivial k (endpoints have one column). At n=6 triple (2,2,2), k=3 matrix has rank six on seven outcomes; two distinct distributions (central probability 2/5 with either six balanced permutations weight 1/10 or three cyclic permutations weight 1/5) give each block counts (0,1,2) with probabilities (1/5,3/5,1/5), hence party marginals (1/5,4/5). This is uniqueness conditional on feasibility, not existence.
residual_risks: The theorem needs exactly three distinct floor levels and strict within-block residues; not a general all-strata result.
